claims.title: Exact minimax regret is a translated optimization over the active fixed-model root frontier
claims.scope: finite fixed-model active-experiment problems with one model selected once, exact rational costs, deterministic public policies, and a model-informed causal oracle
assumptions: the oracle knows the fixed model identity before the horizon
the oracle and shared controller use the same experiment menu, acquisition costs, horizon, hidden dynamics, and zero-error code universe
the active-experiment frontier is complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the oracle does not know future hidden-state or observation realizations
this is minimax regret rather than Bayesian regret
the result is not evidence for simulation

claims.title: Componentwise cost dominance remains valid after subtracting the fixed model-oracle vector
claims.scope: root policy-cost vectors and one fixed vector of model-informed oracle values
assumptions: the same oracle value O_m is subtracted from every candidate policy in model coordinate m
componentwise dominated policies were removed only by non-strict coordinatewise cost dominance
nonclaims: the argument would fail for policy-dependent benchmark translations
Pareto sufficiency does not imply frontier size is polynomial

claims.title: Every shared public policy has nonnegative regret relative to the model-informed causal oracle
claims.scope: fixed-model active-experiment policies where the singleton oracle receives the model identity but no additional future information
assumptions: the singleton oracle may emulate the shared policy
both sides pay identical declared experiment and coding costs
nonclaims: zero regret does not imply the model was identified
the theorem does not compare against a path-clairvoyant oracle

claims.title: The exact minimax-regret policy cannot have larger worst-model regret than the robust-cost optimizer
claims.scope: the same complete active fixed-model root policy frontier under robust-cost and minimax-regret objectives
assumptions: both objectives range over the same deterministic public policies
oracle values are fixed before selecting the regret-optimal policy
nonclaims: the theorem does not assert a strict improvement
the robust-cost and minimax-regret optimizers may coincide

claims.title: Symmetric acquisition-cost accounting prevents artificial model-uncertainty regret
claims.scope: active-experiment regret benchmarks in which controller and oracle face the same compulsory or optional experiment menu
assumptions: the oracle is charged the same acquisition cost for any experiment it selects
the shared controller is charged the declared acquisition cost under the same rule
nonclaims: experiment costs do not generally cancel when oracle and shared controller choose different experiments
the acquisition-cost numbers are declared model inputs

claims.title: One-period no-signal point-mass K3 has exact minimax regret one
claims.scope: three globally fixed point-mass K3 models, one period, one no-signal experiment, and zero acquisition cost
assumptions: binary complete prefix-code length vectors are permutations of (1,2,2)
the model-informed oracle knows which point-mass model is fixed
nonclaims: the value one is specific to this finite instance

claims.title: Source-independent public three-way randomness lowers K3 minimax regret from one to two-thirds without model information
claims.scope: the same one-period point-mass K3 family with a uniform public signal independent of source and model
assumptions: the public signal is observed by the deterministic policy before code selection
the singleton oracle value remains one
nonclaims: the regret reduction is coordination value rather than epistemic information gain

claims.title: Free one-period model revelation eliminates K3 minimax regret
claims.scope: the same one-period point-mass K3 family with a perfectly model-revealing zero-cost experiment
assumptions: the signal arrives before code selection
the model-informed oracle and shared controller use the same code universe
nonclaims: free perfect revelation is a bounded example rather than a claim about real experiments

claims.title: Bounded exact active fixed-model minimax-regret audit
claims.scope: the no-signal, public-randomness, revealing-signal, symmetric-cost, and robust-cost comparison instances exercised by repository tests
assumptions: all active-experiment policy frontiers and singleton oracle solves complete below configured caps
all probabilities and costs use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded finite testing is not a scalability theorem
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation
